t: How many principles of management did Henri Fayol enunciate in his work 'General and Industrial Management'?
e: Fayol listed 14 principles (division of work, authority, discipline, unity of command, unity of direction, remuneration, scalar chain, esprit de corps and others) and five elements of management.

t: A general insurer organises its field operations into Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western zones. This is departmentation by:
e: Geographic (territorial) departmentation suits organisations whose operations are dispersed and need local responsiveness.

t: Which of the following factors permits a wider span of control?
o: Well-trained subordinates performing routine, similar work
A manager with no delegated authority
e: The span can widen when work is routine, subordinates are competent, communication is easy and the manager delegates effectively.

t: Which statement about line and staff authority is INCORRECT?
o: Line authority flows down the chain of command
Staff managers have the authority to issue commands directly to line employees
Staff authority is advisory in nature
Conflict between line and staff often arises from unclear authority
e: Staff functions advise and serve the line; they do not command line employees unless given functional authority for a specific matter.

t: According to the course, which of the following statements about learning is correct?
o: Learning stops once formal education is complete
Only young employees can learn new skills
Everybody learns all the time, regardless of age, and often learns things other than what the teacher intends
People learn only what the trainer intends to teach
e: Learning is continuous and incidental; managers must recognise that employees draw their own lessons from what they observe.

t: Attributing one's own feelings or motives to another person – for example a manager who dislikes paperwork assuming that his staff dislike it too – is the perceptual error of:
e: Projection ascribes one's own characteristics to others; the halo effect generalises one trait and stereotyping generalises a group.

t: Political science is relevant to HRM because:
o: Organisations are political entities in which power and influence shape decisions
It defines the chart of accounts
e: Understanding power, coalitions and conflict helps explain behaviour that purely rational models cannot.

t: Which of the following is NOT a source of perceptual error listed in the course?
o: Role or status of the person observed
e: Perceptual errors stem from role, occupation, appearance, non-verbal cues, limited attention, stereotyping and halo; a written job description reduces rather than causes bias.

t: In the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid, the 9.9 style represents:
o: High concern for task and low concern for people
Low concern for both people and task
High concern for people and low concern for task
High concern for both people and task (team management)
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The grid plots concern for people against concern for production; 9.9 is team management, 9.1 task management, 1.9 country-club and 1.1 impoverished.

t: Under the Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act 1959, an establishment in the private sector must notify vacancies to the employment exchange if it ordinarily employs:
e: The Act requires notification (not compulsory recruitment through the exchange) by public sector establishments and private establishments with 25 or more employees.

t: Which of the following is an external source of recruitment?
e: External sources include advertisements, employment exchanges, agencies, institutions, professional bodies and referrals; promotions and transfers are internal.

t: Aptitude tests used in selection are designed to measure:
o: A candidate's potential to learn or perform a particular kind of work
What the candidate already knows about the company
e: Aptitude tests assess latent ability (numerical, verbal, clerical), whereas achievement tests measure acquired knowledge and medical tests assess fitness.

t: The primary purpose of job evaluation is to:
o: Assess the performance of the job holder
Determine the relative worth of jobs to establish a fair and consistent pay structure
e: Job evaluation rates the job, not the person; performance appraisal rates the person.

t: The steps of the employment process after an offer is accepted are, in order:
e: The new employee is first oriented to the organisation and then placed in the specific job; probation runs after placement.

t: The Apprentices Act 1961 requires employers in designated trades to:
o: Pay apprentices full wages equal to permanent employees
Confirm every apprentice as a permanent employee
Engage apprentices and provide them structured practical training with a stipend
e: The Act regulates apprenticeship training; apprentices are trainees paid a stipend and are not guaranteed employment on completion.

t: In the seminar method of training, participants are often divided into small groups called:
e: Syndicates discuss an assigned problem and present conclusions to the plenary; frames are units of programmed instruction.

t: 'Cognitive knowledge' gained from reading, hearing and seeing is useful only when:
o: It is certified by a university
The person can apply it in practice
It is memorised word for word
It is acquired before the age of 25
e: The course stresses that knowledge becomes competence only through application, which is why doing and reflecting outweigh hearing and reading.

t: In the graphic rating scale method of appraisal, the rater:
o: Ranks all employees from best to worst
Compares each employee with every other employee in pairs
Marks the degree to which an employee possesses each listed trait on a continuum
e: Graphic rating scales are simple but prone to halo and central tendency; BARS adds behavioural anchors to reduce these errors.

t: A branch has sent a clerk on three training programmes but his performance has not improved; the manager discovers he is capable but not interested. Which element of performance is lacking?
e: Performance requires skill, will and support; more training (skill) cannot cure a lack of willingness, which calls for motivation or counselling.

t: The 'custodian of values' within an individual, which 'pricks' when something contrary to one's standards is done, is called:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Values form character and conscience guards them; ethics is the study of right and wrong that these values express.

t: Management development differs from training in that it is:
o: Future-oriented and focused on climate, culture, leadership, vision and strategy
Concerned only with current operational skills
e: Training addresses present job skills; management development prepares managers for broader future responsibilities.

t: Which of the following are elements of organisational climate in Likert's model?
o: Openness, authenticity, belongingness and role clarity
e: Climate is the intervening variable comprising attitudes and perceptions that link causal variables to end results.

t: Organisational culture is defined in the course as:
o: The physical layout of the office
The aggregate of values, practices and beliefs shared in the organisation
The legal form of the company
e: Culture is shaped by senior management's philosophy and reinforced by behaviour; it strongly influences how change is received.

t: Quality of Work Life (QWL) is influenced by three sets of factors. Which of the following correctly lists them?
o: Interest rates, exchange rates and inflation
Individual needs, job characteristics and organisational factors
e: QWL is the interaction between what the individual needs, what the job offers and how the organisation is run.

t: Two development officers have identical targets. Officer A earns ₹60,000 with 10 years' experience and Officer B earns ₹60,000 with 2 years' experience. According to equity theory, Officer A is likely to:
o: Perceive inequity because his input (experience) is higher for the same outcome
Feel fully satisfied because pay is equal
Perceive inequity in favour of himself
Be unaffected because pay is above minimum wage
e: Equity is judged by the ratio of outcomes to inputs compared with a referent; equal outcomes for unequal inputs create perceived under-reward.

t: In McClelland's theory, a manager who enjoys influencing others and taking charge of situations has a high:
e: Need for power (socialised rather than personal) is associated with effective managers; affiliation seeks friendly relations and achievement seeks personal accomplishment.

t: A trainer evaluates a claims-processing training programme by measuring whether the turnaround time of claims improved three months after the course. This corresponds to which level of Kirkpatrick's model?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Kirkpatrick's four levels are reaction (satisfaction), learning (knowledge gained), behaviour (application on the job) and results (organisational outcomes such as turnaround time).

t: Which of the following is a 'safety' need in Maslow's hierarchy?
o: Job security and protection from loss of income
e: Safety needs include physical safety, job security, pension and insurance; this is why statutory social security benefits matter to employees.

t: Removing an unpleasant condition – for example withdrawing close supervision once an employee submits reports on time – to strengthen a desired behaviour is:
e: Negative reinforcement strengthens behaviour by removing an aversive stimulus; punishment weakens behaviour by adding one.

t: Which of the following is the richest communication channel for resolving a sensitive grievance with an employee?
e: Face-to-face communication carries verbal and non-verbal cues and allows immediate feedback, which is essential for sensitive matters.

t: The main purpose of feedback in the communication process is to:
o: Confirm that the message has been received and understood as intended
Avoid the need for a channel
e: Without feedback the sender cannot know whether the receiver decoded the message correctly; two-way communication is therefore more reliable.

t: Instructions issued by the head office to branches on revised claim settlement procedures are an example of:
e: Downward communication carries orders, policies and procedures from higher to lower levels.

t: Under McGregor's Theory Y, managers assume that employees:
o: Must be coerced to put in effort
Avoid responsibility and prefer to be directed
Find work as natural as play and will exercise self-direction towards objectives to which they are committed
e: Theory Y supports participation, delegation and job enrichment; McGregor regarded it as the remedy for the self-fulfilling pessimism of Theory X.

t: In Hersey and Blanchard's model, the 'participating' style is appropriate when the follower is:
e: Telling suits unable/unwilling, selling suits unable/willing, participating suits able/unwilling and delegating suits able/willing followers.

t: Consensus decision-making differs from majority voting in that consensus:
o: Is reached when more than half the members agree
Seeks a decision that all members can accept and support, even if not their first preference
Is decided by the senior-most member alone
e: Consensus builds commitment because no member is outvoted; majority voting can leave a dissatisfied minority.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: Which of the following is a reason the course gives for managers avoiding participative decision-making?
o: Belief that participation always saves time
Fear of becoming redundant if subordinates can decide for themselves
e: Leaders avoid participation when they doubt subordinates' competence, see development as not their job, fear redundancy or think participation wastes time.

t: A leader who makes all decisions himself, gives orders and expects obedience without explanation is exercising which style?
e: Autocratic leadership centralises decisions; democratic leaders consult the group and laissez-faire leaders leave decisions to the group.

t: In the classification (grading) method of job evaluation, jobs are:
o: Slotted into a predetermined number of grades, each with a written description
Compared pairwise with every other job
Evaluated on money values per factor
e: Classification is used widely in government and public sector organisations where grades are defined in advance.

t: The principle of natural justice in disciplinary proceedings requires that:
o: Punishment must be imposed within 24 hours of the misconduct
The employee must be given an opportunity to be heard before punishment is imposed
The enquiry officer must be the complainant
The employee must be dismissed for a first offence
e: Audi alteram partem (hear the other side) and the rule against bias are the twin pillars of natural justice in domestic enquiries.

t: Vigilance departments in public sector insurers and banks function under the overall guidance of the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
e: The CVC supervises vigilance administration in central government organisations and public sector undertakings, including public sector insurers.

t: Under the Industrial Relations Code 2020, a trade union is recognised as the sole negotiating union of an establishment if it has as members not less than:
o: 51% of the workers on the muster roll
e: Where no union has 51%, a negotiating council is formed with unions having at least 20% membership each.

t: Under the Code on Wages 2019, for computing wages, allowances excluded from 'wages' (such as HRA, conveyance, bonus and overtime) cannot exceed:
o: 50% of the total remuneration; any excess is added back to wages
e: The uniform definition of wages across the Codes caps excluded components at 50% so that employers cannot reduce PF, gratuity and bonus by inflating allowances.

t: Under the Employees' State Insurance scheme, the monthly wage ceiling for coverage of employees (as applicable since 2017) is:
e: Employees earning up to ₹21,000 a month are covered; contributions are 0.75% by the employee and 3.25% by the employer.

t: Which of the following statements about the sources of personal values is correct according to the course?
o: Values are inborn and cannot be learnt
Values are acquired only through company training programmes
Values are learnt from family, school, stories and spiritual discourses and together form character
Values are the same as the law
e: Values are standards of right and wrong absorbed through upbringing and culture; conscience guards them.

t: 'I am only following instructions' is cited in the course as an example of:
o: A valid legal defence in all cases
A rationalisation used to justify unethical conduct
e: Rationalisations such as 'it is expected', 'others do it' and 'it won't hurt anybody' allow people to evade responsibility for wrong choices.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: Ethical behaviour, according to the course, ultimately provides satisfaction to:
o: Both the person acting and the others affected
e: Acting ethically brings peace of conscience to the individual and trust from customers, colleagues and society.

t: A study cited in the course estimated that in about 15 years roughly what proportion of jobs in the United States could be automated?
e: The estimate illustrates the scale of technological displacement that HR must plan for through reskilling and redeployment.

t: With the increasing participation of women in the workforce, the course notes that complaints of workplace harassment are rising and that:
o: They are purely a private matter between employees
Such offences are now punishable under law, requiring organisations to have preventive mechanisms
They occur only in manufacturing units
e: The POSH Act 2013 makes sexual harassment an offence and obliges employers to constitute committees, conduct awareness and act on complaints.
